```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
here::i_am("errata.qmd")
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)

out <- function(file) {
  read_csv(here::here("maintained", "output", file), show_col_types = FALSE)
}

figure_3 <- out("figure_3_study1_posterior_probs.csv")
figure_4 <- out("figure_4_study1_mean_outcomes.csv")
figure_6 <- out("figure_6_study2_ate_estimates.csv")
static_simulations <- out("text_study1_static_simulations.csv")

mw_final <- figure_3 |>
  filter(topic == "Minimum wage", batch == 10) |>
  arrange(desc(posterior_prob))

mw_mean <- function(arm_label) {
  figure_4$estimate[figure_4$topic == "Minimum wage" & figure_4$arm == arm_label]
}

republican_ipw <- figure_6 |> filter(type == "Republicans", Estimates == "IPW")
lottery <- republican_ipw |> filter(term == "Lottery")
accuracy <- republican_ipw |> filter(term == "Accuracy")

mw_static <- static_simulations |> filter(topic == "Minimum wage")

fmt <- function(x, digits) sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), x)
```

Three sentences in Offer-Westort, Coppock, and Green (2021), *American Journal of Political Science* 65(4): 826–844, [doi:10.1111/ajps.12597](https://doi.org/10.1111/ajps.12597), state a number or a treatment label that the study's own data do not support. Each is a misstatement in the prose. No conclusion in the article changes, and every figure and table it reports is correct as printed. The corrected values below are computed from a maintained reproduction of the analysis, held at `active-maintenance-aec/offer-westort_coppock_green_2021`, which reproduces all 913 of the article's published table and figure values.

Changed tokens are shown in bold on both sides. Where a sentence contains other quantities, those are reprinted unchanged.

## 1. The estimated mean of the leading minimum wage arm

> The winning arm, by a hair, was Proposal 3 (**B**, without current minimum wage), with a probability of being best of 0.219 and an estimated mean of **0.895** over 183 respondents. (p. 835)

*Corrected:* The winning arm, by a hair, was Proposal 3 (**N**, without current minimum wage), with a probability of being best of 0.219 and an estimated mean of **`r fmt(mw_mean(mw_final$arm[1]), 3)`** over 183 respondents.

The arm with a `r fmt(mw_final$posterior_prob[1], 3)` probability of being best and `r mw_final$cumulative_trials[1]` respondents is Proposal 3 (N), whose inverse-probability-weighted mean is `r fmt(mw_mean("Proposal 3 (N)"), 3)`. The 0.895 printed in the sentence is Figure 4's estimate for Proposal 3 (Y), a different arm, which drew `r figure_3$cumulative_trials[figure_3$topic == "Minimum wage" & figure_3$arm == "Proposal 3 (Y)" & figure_3$batch == 10]` respondents and ended with a `r fmt(figure_3$posterior_prob[figure_3$topic == "Minimum wage" & figure_3$arm == "Proposal 3 (Y)" & figure_3$batch == 10], 3)` probability of being best. Figures 3 and 4 label the two versions of each minimum wage proposal "(Y)" and "(N)", so the "B" in the parenthesis is also an "N".

## 2. The arm carrying the 4.1-point Republican effect

> In this particular case, the adaptive design with the smaller standard error allows us to declare the 4.1-point average effect of the **accuracy** treatment statistically significant (p = 0.014), whereas under that static design the effect would not have attained statistical significance (p = 0.152). (p. 840)

*Corrected:* In this particular case, the adaptive design with the smaller standard error allows us to declare the `r fmt(100 * lottery$estimate, 1)`-point average effect of the **Lottery** treatment statistically significant (p = `r fmt(lottery$p.value, 3)`), whereas under that static design the effect would not have attained statistical significance (p = 0.152).

Figure 6 gives the Republican Lottery arm an effect of `r fmt(100 * lottery$estimate, 1)` percentage points with a p-value of `r fmt(lottery$p.value, 3)`. The Accuracy arm's Republican estimate is `r fmt(100 * accuracy$estimate, 1)` percentage points, in the opposite direction, with a p-value of `r fmt(accuracy$p.value, 3)`. The two preceding sentences and Figure 5 both identify the Lottery as the arm in question. The static-design p-value of 0.152 is left as printed: it comes from a bootstrap the deposited materials do not seed reproducibly, and the reproduction cannot recompute it.

## 3. The share of static minimum wage simulations picking the best proposal

> Treating observed success rates as the truth in simulations of the minimum wage experiment, we picked the best proposal 47% of the time in adaptive experiments and **37%** of the time in static experiments. (p. 837)

*Corrected:* Treating observed success rates as the truth in simulations of the minimum wage experiment, we picked the best proposal `r fmt(100 * mw_static$correct_adaptive, 0)`% of the time in adaptive experiments and **`r fmt(100 * mw_static$correct_static, 1)`%** of the time in static experiments.

The deposited simulations pick the best minimum wage proposal in `r fmt(100 * mw_static$correct_static, 2)` per cent of `r format(mw_static$iterations, big.mark = ",")` static runs, which is `r fmt(100 * mw_static$correct_static, 0)` per cent at the whole-percentage precision the sentence uses. Rounding to one decimal first gives 36.5, and rounding that again gives 37. The other three shares in the same passage round correctly.
